Visual consistency audit

Where Pebble Pit disagrees with itself, found by reading the code and shooting the game (75 findings; canvas: 6 high, 16 med, 11 low · dom: 3 high, 19 med, 20 low). "Canvas" is everything drawn in the yard and the deep; "dom" is the sheets, boards, cards and landing page. Each finding has the rule it proposes. The calls that are a matter of taste are votes on the decisions board; the rest are plain fixes.

high canvas · palette · C01

The spark's mark has four shapes: DOM plus, counter four-point star, casino diamond, glyph plus

CLAUDE.md names the spark as red ✚ and the DOM coin (.spark in style.css) is an 11px plus. The canvas counter in the corner draws a vector four-point star (marks.js drawMark), the casino's bin foot draws a 5-cell diamond while its comment says it uses 'the counter's own shapes', and glyphs.js's pip spark is a 5x5 plus. On the bench screen the DOM counter and the canvas counter stand side by side with different spark shapes.

Proposed rule: The spark is a plus everywhere: one 5x5 cell bitmap (glyphs.js pip 'spark'), drawn by the counter, the casino and the DOM alike.

src/render/marks.js:108-121 src/render/casino.js:434-444 src/glyphs.js:101 src/style.css:569-581
high canvas · palette · C02

Purple means seven things: wizard magic, serpent heal, statuses on the foe, crusher fire, deep light, the gamepad cursor, the capstone rung

config/view.js says purple is 'the only purple in the game', meaning what the wizards throw. On canvas it also marks the serpent's heal (NUM_HEAL_FACES, BAR_HEALED), every status the party lays on the foe (STATUS_FOE, including the physical Bleed and Exposed), the crusher's fire, the creatures' bioluminescence and jelly bodies, the far stream and the giant, the gamepad's selection brackets (PAD_ACCENT), and rung 8's capstone parts on deep props. So purple stands for both the enemy healing and our debuffs on it, in the same fight.

Proposed rule: Purple means magic only, on either side. Statuses on the foe and the pad cursor take ink or white, and heal-versus-debuff is told apart by shape, not hue.

src/config/view.js:56-59 src/config/deepdraw.js:296-297 src/config/deepdraw.js:324-326 src/config/deepdraw.js:404
high canvas · palette · C04

The air filter's dial is a green-amber-red traffic light

DESIGN.md's casino section says 'Black and white, not red and green', calling a traffic-light wheel the first thing to use color for mood. Green and red already mean the farm's spores and the meteor's sparks. DIAL_ZONES paints the filter's dial #3aa655/#e2c12b/#d23b2e. The amber is in no palette, and the green and red are near-misses of the spore and spark tones.

Proposed rule: The dial reads in ink: clean/dirty/filthy as white, grey and black bands (or a SHADES ramp), never a coin color.

src/config/filter.js:45-48 DESIGN.md:305-312
high canvas · variation · C20

Yard buildings and machines are flat #000; the deep's props, plinths, domes and the finale house are grained

The rule says no flat fills. In the deep every built mass is hash-grained (PLINTH_TONES, DOME_TONES, props' toneAt, pods, floor), and so is the finale's house (home.js). In the yard every building is one flat #000: tower (13x34 cells, the largest mass), shack, sheds, filter, casino, houses, garage, bench, outhouse, balloons, shield props, the 'stone' arch. The machines can't be anything else, because drawSprite hardcodes '#000'/'#fff'. house.js and shack.js call the black silhouette the house grammar; apothecary.js grains its hut, but in #000-#151515, which hardly shows.

Proposed rule: Write the split down: yard buildings are flat ink silhouettes (material is dust, sky and ground only), and the finale house and apothecary follow the yard; or grain everything with one tone hook in drawSprite. Pick one.

src/render/tower.js:91-95 src/render/shack.js:25-28 src/house.js:161-171 src/sprites.js:17-31
high canvas · store · C30

Store screenshots are scaled 5/3 and blurred; the capsules are crisp

The five store screenshots are game renders scaled by 5/3, so every 2-px rule is smeared over about 4 px with grey ramps (steamhome.png has about 4,200 colors against 29 in header_920x430.png). The press scanlines are baked in. A player comparing the capsule to the screenshots sees two renderings.

Proposed rule: Store shots are taken at an integer scale with smoothing off (and the press off); a shot has under ~100 colors.

steam/store/screenshots/steamhome.png docs/mocks/steam-capsules-2026-10-12.html:138
high canvas · store · C31

Achievement icons repeat: whole ladders share one byte-identical picture

pickOf strips the rung digits, so PEBBLE0-4 and FIRSTGRAIN are six identical icons, and ROCK0-3, CREW0-3, ORE0/1 and EVERYJOB/WHOLELOT likewise. Steam's list will show rows that look the same. The badge cell is also 16 px on a 24-px glyph cell, a second grid.

Proposed rule: Every icon unique (md5 check in steam-art); a rung carries a rung mark (pips) on the glyph's own cell.

tools/steam-art/picks.mjs:5-6 tools/steam-art/icon-draw.js:18 tools/steam-art/icon-draw.js:62
high dom · color · DOM-01

The landing page's volume slider is the browser's default blue, round control

The held sheet styles its range input (1px ink track, square paper thumb), but that rule is scoped to `.held`; title.css only sizes the slider. On the landing page's settings the volume control renders as Chrome's default blue pill with a round thumb, in light and dark alike, the one saturated non-coin color and the one rounded control on the page.

Proposed rule: Move the range rules off `.held` onto a shared selector (`.held, .col` or a `.range` class) so one slider exists.

src/style.css:1243-1258 src/title.css:69 index.html:93
high dom · state · DOM-02

No focus style anywhere: keyboard focus is the browser's rounded auto ring, text boxes show nothing

There is no `:focus-visible` rule in any of the three sheets. Tabbing the held sheet or the landing column draws Chrome's rounded black/white auto outline (a radius in a square house), and both textareas and the cloud code input set `outline: none` with no replacement, so a focused text box looks exactly like an idle one. `body.pad :focus { outline: none }` hides even that while the pad marker is in use.

Proposed rule: One house focus rule: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 2px }` (square), applied to buttons, textareas and inputs alike.

src/style.css:1201 src/style.css:1213 src/style.css:2184 src/title.css:57
high dom · component · DOM-03

The same sheet button is three heights: 24px held, 27px language list, 29px landing

`.held` sets `font: 12px var(--face)`, which resets line-height to normal, so its buttons are 24px tall (4px 14px padding). The language list re-adds `line-height: 1.4` (27px), and the landing column inherits body's 12px/1.4 plus its own `padding: 5px 14px` (29px). Measured on the live pages: settings rows 24px, language rows 27px, landing rows 29px.

Proposed rule: One `--btn-h`/line-height and one padding for every sheet button; drop the per-page line-height and the landing's 5px.

src/style.css:1035 src/style.css:1216-1233 src/style.css:2195 src/title.css:38-42
med canvas · palette · C03

Four purple families for one meaning

MAGIC_TONES (#9b5de5..#4e2090), ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES (12 rungs sharing only 3 of those values), the finale's FINALE_PURPLE/DARK/LIGHT (#7b3fe4, #3f2378, #b79af2, in none of the others) and the pad's PAD_ACCENT/PAD_DEEP_ACCENT (#6f36c9, #a979ef, 'the capstone purple of shelf.css') are all called 'the' purple. The finale's door and fireworks are visibly bluer than the wizards' rings beside them.

Proposed rule: One purple ramp (ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES); MAGIC_TONES, FINALE_PURPLE* and PAD_* become indices into it.

src/config/view.js:59 src/config/rift.js:170-172 src/config/finale.js:209-211 src/config/pad.js:10-11
med canvas · palette · C05

Tonic colors are near-duplicates of the coin colors, outside FIND_COLOR

The three tonics are tinted #5fb84f, #4a86c7 and #e04848, each a step off its coin's FIND_COLOR ramp (#57c074, #3f68d4/#5b83e0, #e8503a) and in no palette. The fire's fallback is an orange #f5851f that exists nowhere else. On the apothecary the brew reads as a fourth, paler green next to the farm's spores.

Proposed rule: A tonic takes its reagent coin's FIND_COLOR ramp (tonicColor = FIND_COLOR[coin][k]); no tonic literals and no orange.

src/apothecary.js:73-79 src/render/apothecary.js:85 src/config/view.js:61-67
med canvas · palette · C06

Five grey ramps, with near-duplicates one or two steps apart in the same role

The yard's greys are SHADES (#8a8a8a..#111111). Beside them sit FINALE_GREYS ('the yard's greys by name', but #262626..#e3e3e3, none equal to SHADES), the abyss's blue-tinted ABYSS_TONES, AIR_TINTS dust, PAPER, and one-off greys. The one-offs include a mid-grey cluster all meaning 'empty/inactive': #8a8a8a (PORTAL_TORN), #8c8c8c (SEAT_EMPTY_INK, SHELF_INK short), #8f8f8f (HOUSE_CURTAIN) and #909090 (CLOUD_UNDER). Also #a4a4a4 (rain) next to #a6a6a6 (air dust), #aaa (float shadow), #bdbdbd (build ghost), and #3a3a3a (apothecary smoke) next to finale #3d3d3d.

Proposed rule: One yard grey ramp (SHADES extended to paper, about 8 rungs); every grey on the yard canvas is a SHADES index, and the deep keeps ABYSS_TONES as its own.

src/config/view.js:17 src/config/finale.js:208 src/config/rift.js:164-166 src/config/air.js:52-56
med canvas · palette · C07

A radial-gradient vignette and an alpha scanline pattern over every frame

CLAUDE.md says 'no gradients'. press.js lays a createRadialGradient vignette (PRESS_MIX.vignette 0.15) and a 1-px rgba scanline pattern over the finished frame, yard and deep alike. The scanlines put a second tone on every flat fill (rows alternate #111/#101010), and show up in every crop and in the store screenshots.

Proposed rule: Decide it explicitly: either the press is the one sanctioned gradient (written into the rules) or it goes; store shots are taken with it off.

src/press.js:29-68 src/config/piles.js:39
med canvas · palette · C09

Yard alpha fades make off-palette pastels; the deep forbids alpha

rift.js says 'There is no alpha here: a thing fades by being painted in a darker tone of its own family', and the deep keeps that rule. The yard fades by globalAlpha: about 80 sites in sky.js, smog.js, cores.js, crew.js and tower.js, plus the cutscene recede at 35% ink. The results are lavender rings around the tower, pale green and pale blue heaps under the finale, and grey-tinted crew. None of these tones is in any palette.

Proposed rule: A fade steps down its own palette ramp (as in the deep); globalAlpha only for the press and cutscene veils.

src/render/tower.js:137 src/render/cores.js:173 src/render/crew.js:360-369 src/render/recede.js
med canvas · grid · C11

Half-cell eaves, chimney caps and roof lips put 3-px hairlines on the buildings

SHACK_EAVE is P/2, and house.js hangs eaves P/2 past the wall at P/2 tall, with a chimney cap offset P/2. At the device pixel ratio the 3-px lip anti-aliases into a grey edge, visible in the shot as a grey line over the house roof. Everything else on the building is whole cells.

Proposed rule: Lips and eaves are a whole cell (P) or none; nothing on a building is a fraction of P.

src/config/sites.js:88 src/house.js:176-187 src/render/sites.js
med canvas · grid · C13

The deep's giant is drawn on half cells as a flat smooth-edged lozenge

The giant crossing behind the deep is a flat PURPLES[1] fill. Its cell is P*zoom*0.5 and its outline is a sine with hand constants (len 320, r 34, 0.6, 1.2, 6), so its edge reads smooth beside the cell-grid creatures and is one flat tone. That breaks both the grid and the per-cell variation rule. The far stream also uses its own smaller farCell.

Proposed rule: Far things are drawn on the same cell at a darker ramp rung, with hash-dealt tones; depth is tone, not a finer grid.

src/render/fish.js:284-296 src/render/fish.js:263
med canvas · scale · C14

Two number faces on the canvas: a system font at 13 px and the pixel NUM_FONT

Crew counts over stations, the roster's +N and hat counts, and the corner counter are fillText in the page font at 13 px (anti-aliased, off the grid). The status labels use 11 px. The deep's fight numbers and the serpent bar's level use the pixel NUM_FONT at 2 px a font pixel. A count over a shack and a blow's number are both small integers over the world, drawn in different faces.

Proposed rule: Every number drawn on the canvas uses NUM_FONT (at 2 px or at P); text labels stay DOM.

src/render/crew.js:219-234 src/roster.js:646-672 src/render/counter.js:73 src/render/statusicons.js:109
med canvas · line · C16

The pile-full warning triangle is the one anti-aliased, hollow, fractional mark over a station

warning() draws a vector triangle with a stroke r/6 = 2.6 px and a bar and dot sized r/8, r/4 and 0.35r (WARN_R = P*2.6), so every edge blurs and nothing sits on the cell grid. Every other over-station mark (done tick, building glyph, deep choose mark) is solid cells on the grid. style.css copies the r/6 stroke for the .messtag tags.

Proposed rule: The warning mark is a cell bitmap like the other station marks (a hollow 2-px-ruled triangle of whole cells).

src/render/pilemarks.js:40-50 src/render/marks.js:10-27
med canvas · line · C18

Stroked arcs and diagonals in a cell-stepped world: sky ring, benched disc, bridge ramps, casino lever, kit pips

Most rings and diagonals are stepped in cells: flag waves, tower rings, sphere halo, ram wheel, belt ramp, shield braces, filter needle. A few use canvas strokes and arcs that anti-alias: the benched star's skyRing (2 px arc, despite the file's own note that a stroked line would be the only stroke in the sky), the benched disc (filled arc), the bridge ramps (2 px diagonal), the casino lever (a P-wide diagonal stroke) and the kit pips (round arcs, where the serpent bar's pips are square).

Proposed rule: No ctx.arc or diagonal stroke in the world: rings and slopes are cells (the kit's ring() helper and the belt ramp's steps are the models); the rift's deliberate arc stars stay as the one written exception.

src/render/sky.js:31-34 src/render/sky.js:244-252 src/render/sky.js:74-75 src/render/sites.js:78-85
med canvas · variation · C21

Large one-tone masses that are material, not buildings: the muck band, a heap's deep core, the star's crust, the cauldrons

The muck layer can run the world's width as one MUCK_TONE body under a one-tone skin row. A dust heap thick enough to reach SHADES[5] is one flat #111 across its whole core, so the crew scene's rock reads as printed. The star's crust is one deepest red, and the apothecary's 13x10-cell cauldrons are flat sprites beside the grained hut.

Proposed rule: Any mass of material wider than ~4 cells deals its cells from two or three neighboring rungs by a hash (the PLINTH_TONES pattern), including the darkest dust rung.

src/render/smog.js:86-93 src/config/view.js:17 src/grid.js:26 src/render/sky.js:62-64
med canvas · motion · C22

A creature flinching from a hit moves three ways

The serpent's dent is held whole-cell steps. A creature the player clicks eases through a Hermite cubic with a smoothstep blend, and the same creature scared by a lash steps in held floor(age*rate) frames. Whether a creature is touched by a click or a lash changes the animation grammar, not just the reaction.

Proposed rule: Reactions to a blow are held poses with a smear (the serpent's grammar); eased motion only for travel.

src/render/serpent.js:99-118 src/deep/react.js:9-83 src/deep/fauna.js:95-100
med canvas · motion · C23

Five hops, five motion styles

The landing hop is a continuous parabola and the yard dance a continuous |sin|. The finale crowd hops on a held pose table, the abyss-intro hop is a two-state toggle, and the deep-rest hop is physics with drag. A body jumping for joy reads differently in each place it does it.

Proposed rule: A crew hop is one held pose table (the finale's), shared by the dance, the landing and the rest.

src/render/crew.js:647-648 src/crew/dance.js:204 src/finale.js:514-523 src/abyssintro.js:192-194
med canvas · motion · C25

The deep's 'no alpha, fade down the ramp' rule is broken by its own HUD and bodies

rift.js, arms.js, cores.js:97 and riftlife.js all say there is no alpha. Yet globalAlpha fades the serpent's sink veil, fighters and swimmers (bodyInk), deep motes, fight numbers, the whole serpent bar with its heal and shards, and the rift's own twinkle and rings in cores.js, against its own comment. The fight numbers alone fade three ways on one screen: quantized alpha for blows, tone faces plus a 0.5-alpha pop for heals, continuous alpha for bar shards.

Proposed rule: In the deep every fade is a ramp step (ABYSS_TONES / ABYSS_MAGIC_TONES); alpha is reserved for whole-screen veils.

src/config/rift.js:167-169 src/render/cores.js:97 src/render/cores.js:173 src/render/serpent.js:369
med canvas · motion · C26

Shake and flash in the yard against the held-pose, no-flash/no-shake taste

The owner's taste is held poses and held impacts, with no flash, shake or shudder. The yard has a full-window lightning flash, not gated on reduced motion (casino has a mayFlash gate, smog does not). It also has a shield strain shake at sin(now/42), about 3.8 Hz, in whole cells and ungated, a continuous dizzy wobble, a sine-throbbing serpent sink warning, and camera shake on casino hits, the arch catch and summons (that one gated).

Proposed rule: Impacts are held poses; any shake or flash that remains goes through one reduced-motion gate (world.js's), and the strain shake becomes held lean steps.

src/render/smog.js:416-426 src/render.js:311 src/render/shield.js:30-38 src/crew/step.js:131
med canvas · store · C32

Capsule palette and title font are the tool's own, not the game's

The capsules use warm off-whites and near-blacks (#f6f6f4 paper, #efefec earth, #e1e1dd hatch, #141414 ink, #cfc9c4 spray, warm cloud greys) found nowhere in src, where the game is #fff/#000 and neutral SHADES. The title is a private 5x7 bitmap font with a serifed I that the game never shows (in-game the name is DOM monospace text). Its letter cells are 13-20 px, not whole multiples of P. The capsule rock is three concentric noisy bands with no #000 core, unlike the game's depth-shaded rock.

Proposed rule: steam-art imports every color from src/config and shades the rock with depthShade; one title drawing lives in src and both the title page and the capsules use it.

tools/steam-art/capsule-draw.js:18-26 tools/steam-art/capsule-draw.js:44-59 tools/steam-art/capsule-draw.js:151-165 tools/steam-art/capsule-draw.js:202
med dom · component · DOM-04

Held sheet buttons are centered; the landing column's identical buttons are left-aligned

The held sheet and the landing column are built from the same markup (settings, saves, achievements, controls, language, feedback) and title.css says it is in 'the held sheet's hand', but `.held button` is `text-align: center` while `.col button` is `text-align: left`, and the headings follow suit (`.held .word` centered, `.col .word` left). The same settings page reads differently depending on where it is opened.

Proposed rule: Pick one alignment for menu buttons and page words and apply it to both `.held` and `.col` (the landing's left column can keep left only if the held sheet follows).

src/style.css:1232 src/style.css:1120 src/title.css:41 src/title.css:37
med dom · component · DOM-05

Toggle rows have four different 'on' languages

Settings toggles say their state in words ('dark: off') with no visual state; the language list marks the chosen row by inverting it; the feedback form uses a 12px checkbox with an inset square; 'hide finished' goes from dashed to solid border and from .7 to full opacity. Four mechanisms for 'this is on'.

Proposed rule: Decide one toggle anatomy (word plus a box tick on the right, or inversion for 'on') and use it for settings, hide finished and the feedback tick.

play.html:196-206 src/style.css:2196 src/style.css:2206-2212 src/style.css:1424-1436
med dom · component · DOM-06

Four different tick boxes

The feedback tick is a 12px box, 1px border, 2px-inset fill. The objective's quest list uses text glyphs '\u25a1'/'\u25a0' in the 11px face. The barrier bill uses a 7px box with a 1px inset that fades in. The landing foot's cloud mark is a 6px filled/hollow square. None share size, stroke or fill inset.

Proposed rule: One `.tickbox` (size in em so it rides the text size, 1px stroke, fixed inset) used by the form, the quest list and the bill.

src/style.css:2210-2212 src/style.css:2077-2079 src/style.css:2128-2130 src/title.css:88-89
med dom · component · DOM-07

Back rows differ page to page

Most held pages end in a full-width 'back'. The feedback page puts back and send side by side in a half-width pair inside the 26em form, narrower than the sheet. The index on a phone hides the page's back and shows its own small auto-width 'back' inside the list box, top-left. The crashed sheet has none. On the landing page back is a left-aligned row in the column.

Proposed rule: A page foot is always the sheet's width: back alone, or back + the page's action as a `.pair`; the index's inner back becomes the page's back retargeted.

src/feedbackform.js:41-44 src/style.css:2203-2204 src/style.css:1168-1170 src/indexpage.js:79-83
med dom · spacing · DOM-08

The held sheet changes width every time a page is turned

`.held` is sized by its content, so the sheet is 422px of buttons on the front, 190px on settings and language, 354px on saves, 396px on achievements, 312px for the feedback form. Turning a page resizes and re-centers the whole sheet. The landing column, by contrast, holds a fixed `--col-w: 21em` minimum.

Proposed rule: Give the held sheet a fixed min width (the landing's `--col-w`, shared) so pages turn in place.

src/style.css:1023-1039 src/title.css:33 src/title.css:43
med dom · type · DOM-09

Eleven letter-spacing values

Tracking in use: .04em (phone controls), .06em (phone boards), .08em (tip, queue, tile names, ledger labels), .1em (cards, small print), .12em (toast name), .14em (held/landing buttons, raise), .18em (page titles, section signs), .22em (pips), .25em (cloud head), .3em (page words, modal title, pair code), .34em (game name), plus raw `.3em`/`.04em` not multiplied by `--track`. Small print inherits px tracking from its parent, so `.held .small` computes to .168em.

Proposed rule: Four tracking steps as tokens (`--track-0: 0`, `--track-s: .08em`, `--track-m: .14em`, `--track-l: .3em`), always multiplied by `--track`.

src/style.css:1036 src/style.css:426 src/style.css:1365 src/style.css:1416
med dom · type · DOM-10

Five 'small' sizes: 9.84px, 10px, 10.2px, 10.8px, 11px

Small print is written five ways: `.82em` (page notes, pot-picker notes = 9.84px), `10px` (held .small, landing sub/said/foot, objective 'next' tab, skip), `.85em` (shelf tile names, strip = 10.2px), `.9em` (card notes = 10.8px), `11px` (record, quest list, barrier, ledger notes). The measured sweep confirms all five on screen.

Proposed rule: A three-step scale (10px small, 12px body, 17px word, with 14px display) as tokens; replace the em fractions with the token.

src/style.css:370 src/style.css:914 src/style.css:1185 src/shelf.css:178
med dom · type · DOM-12

Labels drop to lowercase in some places and not others

The rule mostly reads 'names and labels upper, sentences lower'. Breaking it: the books ledger's row labels ('pebbles', 'ore', 'playtime') are lowercase and untracked; the index list's names are lowercase; the crew window's section 'the yard' is lowercase (the modal sets no case, so `.rows .sect` inherits none); the mess tags say 'muck'/'poop' lowercase under an uppercase toast name; shelf tags say 'done' and gains 'queued' lowercase.

Proposed rule: Write the case rule down (label = upper + track, sentence = lower + 0) and set case on the component, not by inheritance.

src/shelf.css:610-617 src/shelf.css:653 src/style.css:1141-1146 src/style.css:310-323
med dom · component · DOM-13

Section headings are drawn four ways

Board page title: 12px, .18em, regular, 2px ink rule under. Shelf section sign: 12px bold .18em, inverted ink block, 5px plank above. Ledger section: 12px bold .18em, 1px ink rule under. Rows section in the crew window: inherited case, 1px ink-5 (grey) rule. The modal head title is a fifth: 12px .3em, no rule.

Proposed rule: Two heading levels only: page title (regular, rule) and section (bold, rule or sign, one choice), shared by boards, ledger and windows.

src/style.css:351-359 src/shelf.css:79-94 src/shelf.css:622-632 src/style.css:310-323
med dom · component · DOM-14

Selection lists come in four shapes

Index list: borderless rows, lowercase, 0 tracking, 2px 10px padding, inverted chosen row. Language list: bordered 27px buttons, uppercase, 4px gap, inverted chosen. Saves: bordered subgrid rows, 6px gap, inverted open row, dashed divider before the delete. Pot picker popover: borderless rows, uppercase, 4px 14px 4px 10px. The settings list sits at a 10px gap.

Proposed rule: One 'list of choices' component (row padding, gap, case, inverted chosen) for index, language, saves and the popover.

src/style.css:1144-1147 src/style.css:2194-2196 src/style.css:1447-1475 src/style.css:866-884
med dom · spacing · DOM-17

Border weights: overlays are 1px or 2px with no rule for which

The held sheet, landing column, tooltip and toast are 1px; the board sheet, modal, purse, queue, objective, corner buttons, hop, popover, raise and build button are 2px. The modal's close button is 2px while every button inside a sheet is 1px. Emphasis uses 3px double (goal card, barrier buy) and 3px solid (shelf goal), two ways of saying the same thing.

Proposed rule: Rule it: 2px = something floating over the yard, 1px = a control or a line inside it; one emphasis border (3px double) for goal cards everywhere.

src/style.css:1034 src/title.css:23 src/style.css:1414 src/style.css:1087
med dom · state · DOM-19

Disabled is written three ways, and not at all on the landing page

Board cards go `--ink-5` and dashed; shelf tags dashed and ink-5; the barrier buy ink-5 border; the feedback tick and send drop to `opacity: .4`; the rails' locked arm to `.45`; the dev panel to `.4`. `.col button:disabled` only changes the cursor, so a disabled landing button looks live.

Proposed rule: Disabled = `color: var(--ink-5)` + dashed border, for every control; drop the opacity variants and give `.col` the same.
